newsitem.title: USA: Nextel users rise, scraps roaming charges.
newsitem.headline: Nextel users rise, scraps roaming charges.

text.p: Nextel Communications Inc. on Tuesday said its digital wireless subscribers jumped to 300,300 by the end of 1996 from 85,000 a year earlier.
The company added 72,300 subscribers in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The company also formally launched its service as Nextel National Network, a nationwide digital wireless network which carries no roaming charges.

Roaming is when a subscriber moves beyond their home area, often on to the network of another provider, and most cellular and Personal Communication Services providers charge an additional per minute fee for this service.
Nextel's network currently covers cities where around half the U.S. population live, but is expected to cover 85 percent of the population by end-1998, it said.
A Nextel spokesman said the fourth quarter user figures were better than analysts' estimates, but gave no details.
The company is a specialised mobile radio provider, aiming mainly at mobile workers such as security, airport, hospital and hotel staff and at travelling professionals.
Wireless entrepreneur Craig McCaw is Nextel's largest shareholder. The company also has a large customer base of analogue dispatch radio customers, but gave no subscriber figures.
